parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
The energy cycle shown can be used, along with suitable data, to calculate the enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(g)}$.

Each arrow indicates a transformation, **W**, **X**, **Y** and **Z**. Each transformation consists of one or more steps.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

The following data and data from the *Data Booklet* should be used.

electron affinity of $\text{Cl(g)}$ $= -349\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of atomisation of $\text{Ca(s)}$ $= +193\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of formation of $\text{CaCl}_{2}\text{(s)}$ $= -795\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of solution of $\text{CaCl}_{2}\text{(s)}$ $= -83\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Cl}^{-}\text{(g)}$ $= -364\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the value of the enthalpy change corresponding to transformation **W**. Show your working.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to **(a)(i)** and other data to calculate the value of the enthalpy change corresponding to transformation **Z**.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer to **(a)(ii)** to calculate the enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Write an expression, in terms of **W**, **X**, **Y** and/or **Z**, to show how the enthalpy changes of **two** of the transformations can be used to calculate the lattice energy of $\text{CaCl}_{2}\text{(s)}$.

parts.label: (a)(v)
parts.text:
State whether the lattice energy of $\text{CaCl}_{2}\text{(s)}$ is more or less exothermic than the lattice energy of $\text{MgF}_{2}\text{(s)}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The sulfates of the Group 2 elements vary in solubility down Group 2.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Give the names of **two** solutions that could be mixed to form barium sulfate.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain how the solubilities of the sulfates of the Group 2 elements vary down Group 2.
